open_points.subject: A13 owner-session concurrency
open_points.text: The owner "receives an owner session" at sign-in, but the rules do not say whether another successful sign-in ends an existing owner session or whether several may remain valid concurrently.
open_points.question: What happens to the owner's existing sessions when the owner signs in again?
options: Keep every session independently valid until its own end condition
End all earlier owner sessions
End only an earlier session from the same browser
open_points.default_guess: Keep each session independently valid until its own expiry or sign-out.

open_points.subject: A13 expired confirmation with a different submitted value
open_points.text: Rule 6 says "an expired one is refused and cleared", but later says a submission "giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was"; both apply when the pending value has expired and the submitted value is different.
open_points.question: When a different confirmation value is submitted after the pending confirmation has expired, is the pending confirmation cleared or retained?
options: Check expiry first and clear it
Check equality first and retain it
Clear it but answer only the unequal-value refusal
open_points.default_guess: Check expiry first, refuse, and clear the expired confirmation.

open_points.subject: A15 audit sequence after restore
open_points.text: Sequence numbers are "never reused in a store" and use "the number after the last its store ever wrote", while a restored store "continues from the backup's last number" even though that store may previously have written higher numbers after the backup.
open_points.question: May a restore reuse sequence numbers that were written after the restored backup, or must monotonicity survive restoration?
options: Allow reuse of numbers belonging to rolled-back entries
Keep a counter outside the restored backup and continue above every number ever issued
Treat the restored database as a new store with a distinct lineage
open_points.default_guess: Treat restoration as a new audit lineage and allow reuse only for entries removed by that rollback.

open_points.subject: A16 mapping validation scope
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows "every malformed record and every id that conflicts with one production holds", while rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects "are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported".
open_points.question: Do malformed records and conflicting ids belonging only to unpicked projects appear in the mapping or affect the import?
options: Ignore them completely unless their project is picked
Show them but do not refuse confirmation
Check and refuse the whole file even when their projects are unpicked
open_points.default_guess: Ignore records belonging solely to unpicked projects, except failures that make the file itself unreadable.

open_points.subject: A17 empty store location
open_points.text: Rule 5 says "A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start" and then says "An empty store location is made into a new, empty store" without defining whether "empty" means an empty configuration value, a nonexistent path, an empty file, or an existing store with no records.
open_points.question: Exactly which configured store-location state causes Registry to create a new store, and which states fail startup?
options: Create only when the configured path does not exist
Create for a nonexistent path or an empty file
Treat an empty configuration value as a request to create a store
open_points.default_guess: Require a nonempty configured path and create a store only when no store exists at that path.

open_points.subject: A18 daily run after an import backup
open_points.text: Registry backs up "once a day at 03:00 UTC", while the post-import run is described as an exception and "besides the run after an accepted import, there is at most one run per UTC day"; it does not say whether a successful post-import backup satisfies that day's daily backup.
open_points.question: If the checked post-import backup occurs on a UTC day, must the ordinary 03:00 or startup-catch-up run for that day still occur?
options: The post-import backup satisfies that day's backup
The daily run still occurs, allowing two successful backups that day
It depends on whether the post-import backup occurred before or after 03:00
open_points.default_guess: Count the successful post-import backup as that day's backup and skip another daily run.

open_points.subject: A18 restore recovery-point guarantee
open_points.text: Rule 7 says "a restore loses at most a day of changes" while rule 9 permits the owner to replace the store with "a backup" and does not require the newest checked backup; retained backups may be up to 30 days old.
open_points.question: Which retained backup may the owner restore if the at-most-one-day loss guarantee is to hold?
options: Only the newest successfully checked backup
Any retained backup, with the one-day claim removed or qualified
An older backup only through an explicitly exceptional recovery procedure
open_points.default_guess: Use the newest successfully checked backup for ordinary restoration and treat older backups as exceptional recovery with a larger declared loss.

open_points.subject: A18 failed-run partial files
open_points.text: Rule 6 says "A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file", but no rule defines atomic publication, temporary-file naming, crash recovery, or startup cleanup when the process or host stops during writing, checking, or deletion.
open_points.question: How does Registry identify and handle incomplete backup and decrypted temporary files left by a process or host failure?
options: Write under a temporary name and atomically publish only after the check, cleaning stale temporary files at startup
Record a durable backup state and resume or delete incomplete work
Exclude process and host failure from the no-partial-file guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Use private temporary names, atomic publication, and startup cleanup of stale temporary files.

open_points.subject: A18 restored-state reconciliation
open_points.text: The owner must reconcile retention state before configuring service tokens, but "Registry ... cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done" and A17 allows tokens whenever a later startup configuration is valid.
open_points.question: What prevents service access before the required post-restore reconciliation has actually been completed?
options: Nothing; it is an external owner precondition and not a Registry guarantee
Persist a restore-pending state that blocks service-token startup until explicitly completed
Require verifiable reconciliation evidence before enabling service tokens
open_points.default_guess: Treat it explicitly as an external operational precondition and avoid claiming Registry enforces it.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id collision across projects
open_points.text: A repeat is located by a request id carried by "an existing record of the same model", and on differing facts "the caller reads the record"; for rooms and pointers, the access check is performed against the project supplied by the new call, not necessarily the project of the existing record carrying that request id.
open_points.question: What happens when Kernel supplies an allowed project and a request id already carried by a room or pointer of a different project outside its session's set?
options: Refuse with the ordinary hidden not-found answer and reveal no existing record
Scope request-id uniqueness and lookup by model plus project
Use global request-id uniqueness but return only a generic collision refusal
open_points.default_guess: Scope the lookup to the supplied project and otherwise return the same not-found answer used outside the session's set.

open_points.subject: A04 concurrent revision changes
open_points.text: The rules require a stated revision to equal "the record's current one" and say every action is atomic, but they do not say that checking the revision and committing the change are serialised or performed by a conditional write.
open_points.question: Can two concurrent actions that both state the same current revision both commit, or must exactly one commit and the other be refused as stale?
options: Serialize changes per revised record so exactly one commits
Use an atomic compare-and-change on the revision with the same result
Permit both commits if each saw the revision before either committed
open_points.default_guess: Use an atomic revision compare-and-change so exactly one concurrent change commits.

open_points.subject: M11 uploaded import file disposal
open_points.text: M11 says an uploaded import file is "dropped when the import is accepted", while A16 says an accepted import drops only "the file of the session that confirmed it" and "a file another session keeps stays until that session ends".
open_points.question: When one session accepts the import, are uploaded files in other owner sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end?
options: Drop every session's uploaded import file when the import closes
Drop only the confirming session's file and retain the others
Retain other files only until their next request discovers the closure
open_points.default_guess: Drop every uploaded import file when the import becomes permanently closed.

open_points.subject: M09 post-backup audit entries
open_points.text: The changed model says entries written after the restored backup "are lost with it and exist nowhere", but A18 retains other backups for 30 days and does not say that backups newer than the restored one are deleted; those backups may still contain the entries.
open_points.question: What happens to backups newer than the snapshot selected for restoration?
options: Delete or quarantine every newer backup as part of restoration
Keep them, and change "exist nowhere" to mean absent only from the restored store
Permit them to remain as an alternate audit history with an explicit lineage
open_points.default_guess: Quarantine newer backups and treat them as a separate superseded recovery lineage, not as part of the restored store's audit history.

open_points.subject: M10 migration closure across restore
open_points.text: The changed lifecycle says no backup made before the import "is ever restored", but restoration is an owner action outside Registry and Registry neither records nor verifies which backup the owner selected before startup.
open_points.question: Is the migration closure's permanence only an operational promise by the owner, or must Registry be able to detect and refuse a restored pre-import store?
options: State that permanence depends solely on the owner's external restore procedure
Persist independent evidence outside the backed-up store and verify it at startup
Allow pre-import restoration but require the import closure to be reconstructed before serving
open_points.default_guess: State explicitly that this is an external operational precondition, because the described Registry cannot verify it.
